title: Radioactive decay and carbon-14 dating
caption: Every half-life, 5,730 years for carbon-14, half of the remaining radioactive atoms decay. After 50,000 years only about 0.2% is left, too little to measure reliably, which is why carbon-14 dating works only for remains up to about 50,000 years old.
alt: A curve of the fraction of carbon-14 remaining against time in thousands of years, halving every 5.73 thousand years: 0.5 at 5.73, 0.25 at 11.46 and about 0.002 at 50.
description: The fraction of carbon-14 remaining halves every 5,730 years.
After one half-life, 0.5 remains; after two, 0.25.
After 50,000 years about 0.2% remains: the practical limit of the method.
